newsitem.title: UK: Santer confident EMU will start on time.
newsitem.headline: Santer confident EMU will start on time.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Monday he was confident European Monetary Union (EMU) would begin as planned in January 1999 and that a significant number of countries would join at the start.
Santer dismissed suggestions in a BBC radio interview that even Germany might not be ready in time or that the Maastricht Treaty's criteria for EMU entry would be fudged.
"I am quite confident that it will start on time on the basis of the criteria of Maastricht and with a significant number of member states," he said.
"And even Germany and France -- I am quite confident in that -- they would start in the first wave coming to the monetary union."
The head of the European Union's executive said there was hard work to be done but monetary union would start on January 1, 1999.
"Make no mistake about that," Santer added.
Questioned whether there would have to be fudging if southern European Union countries such as Spain and Italy were to make it in time, he said: "No, we are not fudging the criteria. Not at all."
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday Bonn was on course to join the single European currency and stood by its insistence on a strict interpretation of the entry criteria.

Waigel told parliament that, despite rising unemployment, Bonn would still cut the budget deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, below the three percent target laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
